subject: Nimbus subprocessor addition — flowdown language and approval path
messages:
From: Jane Hamilton <jane.hamilton@edgewave.com>

Cc: Kevin Smith <kevin.smith@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Jun 2025 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Notice: addition of Nimbus AI as subprocessor (data processing for logs)

Hi Kimberly,

Heads up — EdgeWave is engaging a new subprocessor, Nimbus AI (nimbus-ai.com), to handle a portion of ingestion log parsing and replay for our observability product. Nimbus will only process de-identified request logs for feature telemetry; they will not receive customer payloads or PII.

Per our MSA Section 5.2 (subcontracting), we’re sending the formal notice and flowdown package for Redwood review. Attached: subprocessor notice with scope, SOC/ISO attestation references, and a short onboarding checklist.

High-level asks from our side:
- Confirm Redwood’s acceptance of the proposed flowdown language (we included EdgeWave’s standard DPA addendum).
- Any additional audit or encryption terms Redwood requires?
- Required lead time for onboarding (we can hold go-live if you need more review time).

We expect Nimbus to start ingesting test data on 2025-06-20 if all checks pass. If it helps, we can set up a short technical call next week.

Thanks,
Jane Hamilton
Head of Integrations, EdgeWave

Subject: Re: Notice: addition of Nimbus AI as subprocessor (data processing for logs)

Markus / Karthik — looping you in to triage the flowdown package from EdgeWave. Copying Monica for ops impact.

Quick summary: EdgeWave proposes Nimbus (third party) to process de-identified logs. They attached the notice and a DPA addendum draft. Key items I want legal to confirm:
- Acceptable audit rights and frequency (EdgeWave expects annual SOC and random audit access).
- Encryption/KMS expectations — Nimbus claims at-rest encryption and uses a managed KMS; do we require customer-managed keys for this workload?
- Notification timing for future subcontracting — they propose 15 days; per our MSA we generally expect 30 days.
- Any problematic indemnity/limitation carveouts in the DPA addendum.

Ops: Monica, can you advise whether onboarding Nimbus impacts any on-call routing or infra configs (for test ingestion)? If there’s any dependency on our side, flag that and we’ll push timeline.

Jane — thanks for the packet. We’ll aim to respond by EOD Monday (6/9) with a redline and a list of open questions. If EdgeWave needs a go/no-go sooner, let us know.

Best,
Kimberly Park

Date: Fri, 6 Jun 2025 10:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Notice: addition of Nimbus AI as subprocessor (data processing for logs)

Kimberly — thanks for the packet. I reviewed the notice and the proposed DPA addendum. High-level guidance below; I’ve attached a draft with inline redlines (see 20250607-nimbus-dpa-addendum-draft.docx).

Summary / required changes:
1) Notification period: we need a minimum 30 days for new subprocessor onboarding or an exception approval from InfoSec if 15 days is requested. Change the clause to: "Customer (Redwood) to be notified at least 30 days prior to transfer of data to a new subprocessor; emergency exceptions require written InfoSec approval."
2) Audit rights: EdgeWave’s annual SOC + attestation is good, but we require explicit audit rights for any subcontractor processing telemetry tied to our customers. Add: "Redwood (or its designated auditor) shall have the right to conduct an on-site or remote audit of the subprocessor at reasonable intervals upon notice and subject to confidentiality protections."
3) Encryption/KMS: we accept managed KMS for telemetry if they provide evidence of key lifecycle management and role-separated key access. For any production customer data we would require CMEK; for de-identified telemetry, managed KMS with documented controls is acceptable.
4) Flowdown of security obligations: the DPA addendum should require that all obligations in Section 7 (data security) flow down to Nimbus, including breach notification timelines (48 hours) and retention/destruction obligations.
5) Liability carveouts: their DPA had a broad exclusion for metrics/aggregates. Tighten to ensure that resulting misuse that causes downstream customer impact remains covered under indemnity.

Action items:
- Kimberly: confirm the 30-day notification ask and whether we want to run a security intake for Nimbus (I recommend yes).
- Monica / Karthik: confirm if there’s any ops dependency that would delay onboarding past 6/20 — if so, we’ll push the timeline.
- Markus: I’ll send the redline to EdgeWave legal and request a counter-signature pathway (DocuSign).

Quote of proposed redline excerpt to send to EdgeWave (paste into email):
"EdgeWave shall ensure that all subcontractors engaged to process Redwood data are contractually bound to obligations at least as protective as those set forth in the Agreement, including but not limited to: data security measures, breach notification within forty-eight (48) hours, cooperation with audits and investigations, and data retention and deletion obligations. Customer (Redwood) shall be notified in writing at least thirty (30) days prior to any transfer of Customer data to a new subcontractor; emergency transfers require prior written approval from Redwood InfoSec."

I’ll prepare the redline and send to Jane (cc legal).

—Markus
Markus Klein
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Notice: addition of Nimbus AI as subprocessor (data processing for logs)

Jane / EdgeWave Legal — thanks for the packet and for the quick turnaround. Per Markus’ review, Redwood has the following positions we need reflected in the DPA addendum before we can approve:
- 30-day written notice for new subprocessors (emergency exceptions require InfoSec approval).
- Explicit audit right for Redwood (or designated auditor) over the subprocessor.
- 48-hour breach notification flowdown and retention/deletion obligations identical to our MSA Section 7.
- Confirmation of key management controls for Nimbus (we accept managed KMS for de-identified telemetry but need documentation).

We attached a redlined version (Markus’) and a short checklist of security artifacts we need from Nimbus: SOC2 report, data flow diagram, KMS architecture notes, and a brief explanation of their data minimization/retention process. If EdgeWave can return an updated DPA addendum and the requested artifacts, we’ll route for final InfoSec sign-off.

Next steps proposed:
1) EdgeWave to submit updated DPA addendum with the redline accepted/rejected items and attach Nimbus artifacts (target: 2025-06-12).
2) InfoSec review (internal) — target 3 business days after receipt.
3) DocuSign path for the DPA addendum and Order Form amendment (if required).

If EdgeWave can’t meet the 6/20 test ingestion date, we can pause until signatures and intake are complete.

Thanks — looking forward to the updated materials.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Manager, Legal Operations
Redwood Inference
